items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: I came and hung out with Fats.

ctx.x: Yeah, Arthur Caypart. I don't know whether you know him or not. Light-skinned colored fellow that played decent trumpet; nothing to brag about, but a decent trumpet. And me. So the only place I could sit would be between Caypart and Fats, because I wanted to hear Fats myself. Boy, he was so pretty, he played so pretty, I couldn't imagine a cat playing that pretty.

And anyway, Andy said, 'Come on down front,' you know. So I went down in front and I played 'McGhee's Special.' And when I did that, Fats looked at me like that. He said, 'Man, how you do that?' items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: I remember I went back with Kirk, because that's when I met Fat Girl, heh-heh...

ctx.x: No, we weren't in Detroit. We were in Boston. But I had to go to Detroit to get her out on bail, because I didn't know nobody there to send the money to to get her out, and nobody probably would have gone out anyway. But I had to go to Detroit to take care of that.

And when I went back with the band, something funny happened. I don't know what it was. I can't remember what the hell it was. But I didn't stay too long anyway after that. I didn't stay too long there. I remember I went back with Kirk, because that's when I met Fat Girl, heh-heh...

items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: And Fats and I and Ernie Henry. It came out pretty good.

ctx.x: Milt Jackson on piano. Curley Russell on bass, I think -- I'm pretty sure it was. And Fats and I and Ernie Henry. It came out pretty good. The two trumpets was the main issue there anyway. Which I'm grateful that it came out that good.
